strongest_for: The idea addresses a documented, real failure mode and proposes a controlled test of it. NSM shows that multi-hop KBQA loses accuracy because intermediate supervision is missing and spurious paths reach the right answer (C007, C008), and KG-Hopper states that step-isolated pipelines cause error cascades (C007). Meanwhile the context family demonstrably helps: GNN-RAG gains 8.9-15.5 F1 on multi-hop/multi-entity questions by supplying path context (C006), and SG-RAG MOT improves MetaQA answers by merging and ordering retrieved triplets (C003). Critically, no retrieved work performs a matched-budget isolated-vs-context comparison at the level of the supervision signal, and none commits to reporting a negative result. Even a null result (context does not help once tokens are matched) would be a useful, currently missing data point, and the hop-transfer framing is genuinely under-specified in the literature (C009).
strongest_against: The mechanism is not clearly novel and is at risk of being un-attributable and infeasible in the setting where the baselines live. Subgraph context for LLM KGQA is already established: GNN-RAG verbalizes retrieved shortest paths as LLM context (C006), SG-RAG MOT merges and orders triplet subgraphs (C003), and DrKGC already integrates a retrieved subgraph into LLM *fine-tuning* via a GCN adapter (C005). So the idea's distinctive claim collapses to two moves: (a) source-passage provenance as the context source, and (b) moving context construction from inference into the training supervision. (a) is unavailable on the standard benchmarks every baseline uses — WebQSP/CWQ are Freebase-based (C001, C013) — and (b) is a modest relocation whose measured effect is confounded with simply supplying more supervision tokens, which the literature itself views as double-edged (C004 vs. C003; C014). The repair loop and lower-hop RL are separately precedented (C007, C012), and the repair loop rests on an unevidenced locality assumption (C010). Running all three stages also requires the unevidenced assumption that they are independently ablatable (C011), and the central hop-transfer claim has no comparable published protocol (C009).
most_important_unresolved_question: Is there any dataset where triples carry source-passage provenance, the standard multi-hop KGQA baselines apply, and matched supervision budgets can be enforced — so that passage-context supervision can be compared fairly against the strongest existing methods? If no such setting exists, the central mechanism is untestable as stated and the research question must be reformulated (e.g. onto text-derived KGs, or redefined as training-time graph-neighbourhood context with an explicit differentiation from subgraph-conditioned fine-tuning).
most_dangerous_confounder: Supervision budget. Attaching co-passage triples to every supervision signal increases the number of triples and tokens per example, so an accuracy gain can be produced by the larger context/supervision budget rather than by passage-context relevance. The literature is directly contradictory on this point (SG-RAG MOT: merging overlapping subgraphs helps; DrKGC: overly long inputs introduce noise), so without matched example counts, matched token counts, and an equal-length irrelevant-triples control, the headline effect is uninterpretable (C014).
closest_work_explanation: DrKGC (arxiv:2506.00708) is the closest in mechanism: it learns structural embeddings and logical rules, retrieves a query-specific subgraph, runs a GCN adapter over it, and integrates the result into the prompt for LLM fine-tuning (C005) — i.e. graph context already enters fine-tuning, though for KGC rather than KGQA and without passage provenance. GNN-RAG (doi:10.18653/v1/2025.findings-acl.856) is the closest in the 'context beyond the single path' idea: a lightweight GNN scores nodes and the shortest paths to candidate answers are verbalized as LLM context, giving 8.9-15.5 F1 gains on multi-hop/multi-entity questions (C006), with an explicit limitation that the retrieved subgraph may not contain the answer under entity-linking errors (C002). SG-RAG MOT (doi:10.20944/preprints202505.1992.v1) is the closest to the specific operation of merging/ordering multiple triplets as context and shows it improves MetaQA answers (C003). NSM (arxiv:2101.03737) is closest in motivation: missing intermediate supervision produces spurious multi-hop reasoning, and it is one of very few papers to address the training signal itself (C007/C008).
potential_contribution: If scoped and controlled, the defensible contribution is a controlled study of training-time context supervision: (1) a matched-example, matched-token comparison of isolated triple/path supervision vs. co-passage context supervision that includes an equal-length irrelevant-triples control, on a provenance-bearing KG, with the strongest available baselines (DrKGC-style subgraph fine-tuning, GNN-RAG-style retrieval context, and an NSM-style intermediate-supervision method) reproduced under identical budgets; (2) evidence on whether any benefit transfers to held-out deeper-hop queries under a pre-registered hop split; (3) an honest negative result if the context regime does not beat the matched controls, plus an error-type breakdown (base-fact vs. retrieval/entity-linking vs. composition) that tests whether one-hop failures localize bad facts. What should be dropped or demoted unless it earns its keep: the wholesale 'all co-passage triples' enrichment without relevance selection, and the combined pipeline as a single claim.
overlap_summary: Substantial on the context family and on evaluation: presenting subgraphs/paths beyond the target triple to a language model is standard and effective (GNN-RAG shortest-path context, SG-RAG MOT merged/ordered triplet subgraphs, GRAG textual subgraphs), and DrKGC already couples a retrieved subgraph to LLM fine-tuning via structural embeddings (C003, C005, C006). Evaluation overlap is high with the KGQA family (MetaQA/WebQSP/CWQ, answer-F1/Hits@1) (C001). The RL component overlaps KG-Hopper/KG-Reasoner, and the intermediate-supervision motivation overlaps NSM (C007, C012).
distinction_summary: The only distinctions not covered by retrieved work are: (i) the context source is the supervision triple's own source passage rather than a query-time retrieval or mined logical rules; (ii) the context is part of the training supervision signal and the study is explicitly a matched-budget isolated-vs-context comparison with a negative-result commitment; (iii) a one-hop-failure repair loop and a held-out-hop transfer protocol are combined with the context regime. Distinction (i) is at present infeasible on the standard benchmarks (C013), and (ii) is close to an implementation-level relocation of DrKGC's context injection (C005), so the distinction must be demonstrated empirically rather than asserted.

novelty.question: Has essentially the same idea been proposed?
novelty.finding: The general mechanism (give the LM more than one triple of context, up to and during fine-tuning) is already established. DrKGC integrates a retrieved subgraph into LLM fine-tuning via a GCN adapter, GNN-RAG supplies shortest-path context, and SG-RAG MOT merges/orders triplet subgraphs. The idea's uncovered element is only the provenance-derived, supervision-level framing.

novelty.question: Is the difference only implementation-level?
novelty.finding: The delta vs. DrKGC is thin: both fine-tune an LLM with subgraph-derived structural context. The differences (passage provenance instead of rule-guided retrieval; context attached to the supervision signal instead of the inference prompt) are real but implementation-level until shown to change what the model learns, and the auxiliary repair and RL components are separately precedented (NSM; KG-Hopper).

novelty.question: Is any version of the specific hypothesis (passage-context supervision, matched budget, hop transfer) already tested?
novelty.finding: There is no retrieved work in the searched set that trains on co-passage triples as supervision with matched-budget controls, so the specific hypothesis is at least untested; but the burden is on the idea to show the effect exceeds the context-quantity effect that prior work already reports as double-edged.

technical_validity.question: Does the mechanism's precondition (passage provenance for supervision triples) hold in the intended evaluation setting?
technical_validity.finding: The mechanism's precondition — triples linked to a shared source passage — fails on the benchmarks every baseline uses. WebQSP is built on Freebase and CWQ is derived from it; MetaQA is a synthetic graph. The idea must either find a provenance-bearing KG with comparable baselines or redefine 'context' as graph neighbourhood, which is already occupied by subgraph retrieval work.

technical_validity.question: Are one-hop failures diagnostic of bad base facts, so corrective examples can fix them?
technical_validity.finding: The repair loop assumes one-hop failures localize incorrect base facts. But documented failure sources are retrieval coverage and entity linking (GNN-RAG limitation) and missing intermediate supervision (NSM) — not necessarily false triples. If one-hop errors are dominated by these, corrective examples target the wrong object and may teach the model to fit noise.

technical_validity.question: Which co-passage triples are reasoning-relevant, and does the mechanism need relevance selection?
technical_validity.finding: Co-passage triples are topical by construction; the idea defines no relevance criterion for which co-passage triples to include, while prior work is split on whether extra context helps or injects noise. Without a selection rule (or an ablation over selection rules) the mechanism is underspecified.

experimental_validity.question: Could the claimed result be produced by a confounder such as a larger supervision/context budget?
experimental_validity.finding: Supervision-budget confound: the treatment arm sees more triples/tokens per example, so gains may come from the larger budget. The required controls (matched examples, matched tokens, equal-length irrelevant-triples arm) are stated in the idea's own variables but are hard to satisfy jointly with a fixed data budget, and the literature provides conflicting expectations.

experimental_validity.question: Is the deeper-hop transfer metric specified and comparable to prior work?
experimental_validity.finding: The headline hop-transfer claim has no directly comparable baseline: no retrieved work reports an explicit train-on-shallow/test-on-deeper-hop protocol. The evaluation will therefore need a bespoke split, and improvements cannot be read against published numbers.

experimental_validity.question: Are the baselines strong and are budgets matched across arms?
experimental_validity.finding: Baselines must be strong and budget-matched: the natural comparators (NSM intermediate supervision; GNN-RAG retrieval-context; DrKGC subgraph fine-tuning) were developed on different KGs, metrics and splits, so a fair comparison requires re-implementing them under the idea's matched regime — a substantial effort that, if skipped, would make any gain unconvincing.

practicality.question: Is the three-stage pipeline feasible and attributable within a realistic compute and data budget?
practicality.finding: The full pipeline requires building a provenance-bearing KG, running two matched fine-tuning regimes, an iterative repair loop, and an RL stage — each needing its own ablation to attribute effects. The idea assumes these stages are independently runnable under a fixed budget without evidence.

practicality.question: Is the required data resource available or must it be built?
practicality.finding: Data-engineering cost: constructing a KG whose triples are linked to source passages, with train/dev/test splits and question sets comparable to MetaQA/WebQSP/CWQ, is a non-trivial resource-creation effort that is not a standard artifact in this literature.

practicality.question: Is the outcome useful even if the hypothesis is false?
practicality.finding: A negative or null result is explicitly committed to and would still be informative (no retrieved work tests matched-budget passage-context supervision), which lowers the practical risk of the investigation even if the hypothesis fails.

status_rationale: The idea targets a real documented failure (spurious intermediate reasoning, step-isolated error cascades) and proposes something the retrieved literature does not test — a matched-budget, supervision-level isolated-vs-context comparison with a repair loop and a hop-transfer protocol (C003, C007, C009, C014). But the overlap is substantial: subgraph context for LLM KGQA is established and DrKGC already injects a retrieved subgraph into LLM fine-tuning (C005, C006), so novelty reduces to a thin, implementation-level relocation plus a context source (source passages) that is unavailable on the standard benchmarks every baseline uses (C001, C013). The remaining components are separately precedented (C012) and the repair loop rests on an unevidenced locality assumption (C010). This is not clearly flawed — the confounder is controllable and the feasibility problem is addressable by changing datasets — but it cannot be judged novel or promising until (i) a provenance-bearing evaluation setting with strong, budget-matched baselines is identified, and (ii) the context effect is shown to survive matched-token and irrelevant-context controls. Hence promising_needs_validation rather than substantial_overlap or weak_or_flawed.
